event: For eleven years Lessa Orvane has mapped places she never saw, better than those who had.
Her Lenn Pass map, drawn from notes and inference, beat the survey it was based on.
Measurement records where things are; understanding predicts where they have to be.
A freight agent mentions the dungeon to her as an administrative anomaly.
Eleven days later the pull comes, so faint she takes it for professional curiosity.
She finishes her drainage map for a mining consortium and starts north.
It stays a low incompleteness, a place she has not mapped; she always fills the gap.
After four days on foot she assesses the camp from the ridge: distances, angles, function.
Everything in the camp faces the hole, like a compass needle facing north.
"Lessa Orvane." "Purpose?" "I make maps." "Of the dungeon?" "Of whatever is there."
She asks to see his structural data; he closes the book. "The data is mine."
"I'm not going to take it. I want to cross-reference it." "With what?" "With my map."
She reads his name, Osren, from the signature at the top of his book's first page.
She surveys the entrance: 3.4 meters tall, 2.1 wide, in a basalt plug older than the ridge.
By midday she has a site plan of the camp, with contours and the outward warm wind.
Dalya, splicing rope on a crate, says she has drawn the fire three feet too near the entrance.
Lessa measures; Dalya is right. "You're good at this." "I know."
On the second day Osren lets her read the structural columns, not the names.
Seven of eighteen entries have depths; the deepest return was a mason, eight years ago.
From the entrance bearing and the warm air she sketches four nested chambers round a basalt core.
"You cannot know that." "I can't confirm it. The geometry is constrained."
Osren opens his ambient observations, which no one has asked to see, and turns them to her.
"May I copy this?" "Yes."
On the third day she annotates the blank cloth in HB charcoal, the hardest grade.
She draws, not writes: the Gullet's first sixty meters, a side passage, the arch, Warrens angles.
It is the first time anyone has used the cloth as a map.
The gap past the arch cannot be filled from outside; three days have confirmed it.
She packs her case, charcoals by hardness, four sheets of vellum, and stands at the entrance.
"Voluntary," she tells Osren. "Are you sure?" The pull is mild; she could turn back.
She cannot fill the gap from outside. "Yes." She goes in.
The ribbing is 2.3 meters apart, as she predicted; the side passage at 39 meters, not 40.
The walls pulse by millimeters in a forty-second cycle she did not predict.
She reads the inscriptions: eighteen names and one gap. She would be the first something.
She maps the arch at 310 meters, the first human structure inside, in full elevation.
Crossing it, she notes the keystone has settled about 0.3 millimeters since it was built.
The Asking comes as a spatial proposition: how deeply do you understand space?
The Ledger names her The Survey, with the Gift True Bearing: every space she enters, known.
Its Cost is The Reference: her inner map is her only reference; she will follow it over reality.
The Ledger reads Vitality 9, Resolve 18, Attunement 12, Fortune 11.
Compelled, mildly, at sixty miles; the Maw is unsure why it reached so gently.
The cartographer's fundamental vulnerability, expressed as a gift.
At the Warrens' threshold True Bearing unrolls the whole labyrinth in her mind, 340 by 220 meters.

changes.note: True Bearing mapping of the Warrens, Attunement +1

event: She touches the wall: warm, smooth, faintly yielding, its grain like the rings of a long bone.
The walls of the Marrow Warrens are fused bone; the dungeon is a body, the names anatomical.
The Ledger: Depth 2, the Marrow Warrens, Resolve +1, now 19.

changes.note: Depth transition into the Marrow Warrens, Resolve +1

event: She maps systematically, marking junctions in 6B charcoal for whoever comes after.
She maps the journal, 47 meters in, without reading it: she is a mapper, not a reader.
She maps the pattern room, 4.2 by 3.1 meters, and cross-hatches it as human-modified.
She maps fourteen dead ends in the upper Warrens.
Their bone is rougher, pitted with cavities three millimeters wide and deep.
She notes them and leaves them for the return pass: correct procedure, and her death.
After ninety minutes True Bearing shows Junction 7 at 68 degrees; she drew it at 71.
She goes back, measures 68, and corrects the vellum with the time and the delta.
A passage of 12.4 meters is now 11.9; a dead end of seven meters is now nine.
The Warrens are shifting: a labyrinth that is also alive.

changes.note: True Bearing detection of the Warrens' shifting, Attunement +1

event: She begins a correction log, to map the movement as well as the space.
After two hours: forty-seven corrections, shifts spreading from the deep sections upward.
In the lower Warrens True Bearing rewrites itself continuously as the passages flex.
Her vellum, corrections over corrections, maps a place that no longer exists.
She closes the case: True Bearing is perfect, but it is hers alone, and ephemeral.
Dead end 23, seven meters two hours ago, now shows fourteen.
The way to Depth 3 is open in the northwest; she is a mapper, and she goes back.
The cavities now cluster in inward-angled radial arrays, and the air smells alive.
The concave terminal wall is a trap, its thousands of cavities full of something pale.
A flat, bone-white parasite with starfish digits emerges two meters ahead.
A second, a third, emerging like water from a sponge; five meters ahead and closing.
She turns, and The Reference takes hold: her map says the junction is seven meters back.
She walks seven meters and reaches a wall that was not there ninety seconds ago.
The fresh bone is smoother and softer; the Warrens have sealed the passage behind her.
The new map shows no exit; the old map, which she must follow, shows a junction here.

changes.note: True Bearing mapping of the parasite gallery, Attunement +1

event: She follows the old map, pressing against bone that does not yield.
Behind her the parasites move with a soft hydraulic whisper, three meters off.
She takes out her last vellum and 2B charcoal and draws what will not change: the pattern.
Dead ends are traps, cavities are nests, and a sealed passage sets the parasites loose.
The first parasite reaches her boot.
They are not predators but the immune system; the dead ends are where the Warrens digest.
She is the raw material. She keeps drawing as they separate tendon from bone up her legs.
She finishes, puts the map in the case, and stands the case upright, flap facing out.
The charcoals are still in order: 6B, 4B, 2B, HB.
She trusted the map; she always trusted the map.
The gap is filled: some spaces cannot be mapped. She knows it, and records it anyway.

changes.note: Lessa dies to the bone parasites in dead end 23, Vitality 9 to 0

event: The death report: Lessa Orvane, the Survey, Depth 2; bone parasites, eight minutes after sealing.
The first death caused by the parasites alone.
Both maps were accurate when made; she followed the older, as the Cost required, and would have.
Her Memory Crystal is ivory, precision: a colour and a category new to the Maw.
Her map case holds four sheets, the dead-end analysis among them; the camp plan too.
Her 6B survey lines remain at seven junctions of the upper Warrens.
The Warrens' shifting is documented for the first time.
The Maw reached for her gently because it wanted a map: to see itself described.
It sees itself as in a portrait: recognisable, slightly wrong, and fascinating.
Osren writes: Lessa Orvane, cartographer, voluntary; purpose, to map. Did not return.
Her marks are the first on the cloth that can be used: navigation, not memorial.
The fire still burns, and the blank cloth has a map on it now. 981 remain.
LESSA ORVANE — DEPTH 2 — FIRST TO MAP.
